categories.summary: The run of big overseas hacks and outages continues, and the collector still ranks the suspected China campaign as strong and touching Australia; governments have blamed China for some of it, but no Australian attack in it is confirmed. drivers: A run of big overseas hacks and outages continues: this week the EU Commission confirmed a data leak from an ongoing attack, after Visa/Mastercard/JPMorgan suppliers, the FBI crime database, Chase, Apple and Microsoft. None has hit Australian banks, phones or power.

Governments have blamed China for some of this hacking, which now uses AI tools to find software flaws fast. If it is one deliberate campaign, the likely aim is quiet footholds in allies' phone, power and water networks ahead of any Taiwan crisis, with phone networks, utilities and ports the likely next targets; this is a hypothesis.
Suspected Iran-linked attacks on shop freezers and small water systems remain in Europe and the US.

headline: Iran says three more tankers caught fire after hitting mines in Hormuz, and President Trump says new US strikes may wait until after New Year if there is no deal.
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three oil tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz today; this is Iran's own claim and no one else has confirmed it yet. No new attacks on US bases were found. Trump has threatened to sink Iranian ships that test the US blockade, but says he may hold off new strikes until after New Year. Oil eased again to about US$86, so pump prices should keep drifting down. Fire danger in the Hills is only Moderate today and tomorrow, and Australian phones, banks and power are normal.
